# Discussion

The current evidence supports three bounded conclusions. First, small-variant SNV
performance is strong in the recorded gene-body comparisons, whereas indels remain
a material weakness. Second, the CIGAR path produces useful HBA deletion evidence,
but its present sample set is comparator-selected and cannot estimate sensitivity
or specificity. Third, the assay-aware model exposes physical observability,
intrinsic ambiguity and no-call states that generic caller aggregation does not
represent.

The strongest scientific limitation is not implementation time. It is the absence
of an accessible exact-assay cohort combining raw amplicon reads with independent,
event-appropriate truth. HPRC and GIAB address sequence and WGS-caller questions;
DRAGEN and vendor output are comparators; public unlabelled amplicon reads address
assay mechanics. These roles must remain separate.

The next decisive experiment is a blinded assay-matched panel retaining negatives,
failures and no-calls. Small variants require independently validated sequence
genotypes; alpha deletions require event-specific breakpoint evidence; gains need
dosage plus junction/copy-order evidence; and novel products require independent
confirmation. Product-efficiency/dropout calibration must be fitted on separate
controls before that held-out evaluation.
